wizardofodds_nba_live.note: The NBA feed as the website serves it: the released rows, their manifest and the current pointer at the served root rather than beneath a canary subpath. Fully addressed and fully disabled. Publishing here needs modes.live.state set to ENABLED in a reviewed commit, NBA_PROP_WOO_PUBLISH set to that same state and NBA_PROP_WOO_PUBLISH_APPROVAL set to the approval token, and the switch commits none of those. note: destinations.live stays null because that slot is the unnamed, local-directory one: a remote destination is addressed by name, so reaching a real host is never what a mode resolves to by default. The live addresses themselves are no longer missing. named_destinations now holds wizardofodds_nba_live and wizardofodds_nba_player_props_page_live, which are the served feed root and the served page root, fully described and fully disabled: the publisher refuses live mode on the committed switch alone, before it resolves a destination at all, so a complete address is not an approval and was never the thing standing between this repository and publishing. What remains missing is in missing_external_facts, and all of it is a decision. canary.root stays null for the narrower reason it always did: the default canary writes a local scratch directory the operator names per run with --destination-root.
secrets: No credential material is recorded here and none belongs here. A remote destination names the environment variable its private key is read from, and the key itself reaches the publisher only through that variable.
